transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-14
Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee, Priya Nair, Samir Patel (Redwood); Maya Thompson, Carlos Rivera, Leah Kim, Omar Aziz (Halo Ventures)

Summary: quick QBR, some noisy lines, agenda: usage/costs, reliability, security, next steps.

00:00 Jordan (Redwood AE): okay good afternoon everyone thanks for joining for the QBR, um we'll run through the last quarter's usage and then go into reliability and the roadmap, Priya you wanna kick off with adoption numbers?
00:14 Priya (CSM): yeah thanks Jordan, hi Maya Carlos Leah, we see about a 42% increase in chat sessions month over month, embeddings also up by 28% as you moved the recommender to embeddings pipeline, average tokens per session is trending up also so that's a key driver of costs, there's a note in the dashboard where we saw a sustained token tail after 10pm their time so your batch jobs are spiking.
00:41 Maya (Halo): yeah that's correct, we rolled out longer context prompts for the assistant in July, and some workflows also keep the conversation history in the prompt, we probably need to trim or move to KV cache but we haven't standardized the prefix caching yet.
01:02 Samir (SE): right so quick note on KV cache - sorry sometimes transcripts say K V cash - but the runtime supports prefix/KV caching, we can push more of the session state into the KV cache which will reduce tokenization across repeated context, that should shave token volume and latency, but it will change your cache hit patterns so we should test it on a staging workload.
01:25 Carlos (VP Eng): latency has been fine for most pages but we did notice two incidents in August where p95 spiked to 1.4s from 600ms for the assistant endpoint, those correlated with an autoscaler bounce and a sitewide degrade. Any updates on root cause?
01:44 Samir (SE): yeah we dug in - that was during a burst of long-generations and a model fallback exercised a larger variant, the smart routing ended up routing to a dedicated pool that was near capacity, the fallback triggered a larger model which consumed more GPU memory causing slower scheduling. We pushed a tweak to the routing policy and increased burst headroom on your dedicated pool, but we also recommend adding an explicit fallback budget to avoid large-model fallbacks in production.
02:12 Leah (SRE): okay that matches our outage tickets, we also saw a couple of checksum spikes on the node network, could be infra layer, we manage some of the infra via your dedicated offering?
02:25 Jordan (AE): right so for Dedicated you get reserved capacity and isolation, but if you want even more control we can talk about the Private deployment with a customer-managed VPC, there we hand over the control plane and integrate with your KMS/HSM, logs to your SIEM, that route tends to be slower to onboard but gives extra network control.
02:49 Maya: security is a must for us, SOC2 and SSO are table stakes, we also need audit logs for model access and per-route RBAC - do you have that?
03:00 Priya: yes we do, we have per-route dashboards and audit logs that can be shipped to your cloud account, and we support SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning. I'll share the security pack, we recently completed SOC2 Type II and ISO attestation for the control plane.
03:15 Maya: great please send that.
03:18 Jordan: note - the security docs are in the folder we shared but Priya will send the direct links.
03:24 Omar (Product): quick question on cost optimization - we've seen a 35% increase quarter-over-quarter in hosted costs. Is quantization something worth exploring?
03:36 Samir: yes quantization profiles can give 2-3x perf/cost improvements for certain transformer families, we also have recommendations in Redwood Optimize for batching and token caching, sometimes moving to a 4-bit or 8-bit quantized model for non-critical outputs is a good tradeoff. We can run a quality regression test on a sample of your prompts.
04:00 Carlos: and how about model rollouts - we need stable canaries, we've had an incident where a new model variant produced hallucinations affecting our agent responses.
04:12 Samir: we support canary and A/B rollouts with automatic rollback on quality/regression alerts. It's tied into your eval set; if quality drops beyond your threshold it will revert. We can add tighter thresholds for your prod routes.
04:26 Maya: I want the step-by-step for setting thresholds.
04:29 Priya: we'll include a runbook + recommended thresholds based on your usage profile.
04:35 Jordan: circling back to pilot - you mentioned exploring Dedicated next quarter, what's the timing?
04:40 Maya: budget approvals in Oct, so we'd like a pilot in late October or early November, could be a 3-week POC to validate throughput and latency on your dedicated pool.
04:52 Jordan: sounds doable. Samir can you run a throughput benchmark and simulate our mix (short chat + long-generation + embeddings)?
04:59 Samir: yes I'll set up a 10k-token throughput test, include embeddings at 60k QPS simulated? sorry numbers, but we'll mimic your proportions and share a detailed spreadsheet.
05:12 Maya: we'll also provide a sanitized sample of traffic and SLO targets.
05:18 Carlos: pricing - we need committed vs on-demand pricing options and the delta for reserved capacity, also any discounts for multiyear?
05:28 Jordan: we'll send updated pricing tiers: on-demand hosted, monthly reserved Dedicated tiers (X,y,z), and a committed annual discount table, plus pricing for Private with support tiers. I'll include examples using your current and projected usage so you can see the delta.
05:44 Leah: regarding reliability, can you summarize the mitigation steps for the autoscaler noise?
05:49 Samir: sure, short version: increase scale headroom, tune continuous batching to avoid large scheduling stalls, and add a fallback policy that prefers smaller model variants rather than immediate larger fallback. We also suggest sticky routing for warm KV caches on long sessions.
06:08 Maya: sticky routing sounds useful, will it increase cost?
06:12 Samir: slightly, because warm instances are kept longer, but it reduces cold-starts and long tail latency; often net cost goes down due to fewer retries and reduced token reprocessing.
06:26 Omar: any notes on data residency? we have EU users, how do you handle that?
06:31 Priya: we have region controls and can pin routes to specific regions; with Private you can keep everything in your VPC and region. For hosted we have EU regions and contractual data residency options.
06:45 Maya: good.
06:47 Jordan: quick callout about integration friction - we've seen customers struggle with prompt engineering and pre/post processing, our Solutions Engineering team can provide a short engagement to help optimize prompts and caching strategies.
06:59 Maya: that could be helpful, budget permitting.
07:04 Priya: also a health check runbook - we'll provide a quarterly checklist and alerting templates.
07:10 Maya: nice.
07:13 Jordan: any competitive activity we should know about?
07:16 Carlos: they evaluated Bedrock earlier this year, and Eng did some bench with Anthropic for chat, but the decision factors were SLA and integration speed.
07:27 Jordan: understood, we'll highlight our SLA and dedicated options in the follow-up.
07:32 Priya: ok let's recap next steps - Priya to send SOC2 + security pack, Samir to run bench, Jordan to send pricing and SOW draft, Maya to share traffic sample and SLOs.
07:46 Maya: correct.
07:50 Jordan: thanks everyone, we'll target the pilot kickoff late Oct pending budgets, we'll follow up via email with the artifacts.
07:58 Carlos: thanks.
08:00 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: a few mis-heard words (KV cache as K V cash), some speaker overlaps marked as short cut-offs. References: shared folder link (https://redwood.app/h/halo-qbr) - Priya to email direct links.

Attachments referenced: QBR deck; security pack (SOC2/ISO); benchmark spreadsheet template; pricing sheet (to be sent).

End of transcript.
